papers.title: Immunoinformatics-Guided Design, Immunological Evaluation, and Macrophage Transcriptomic Profiling of a Multi-Epitope Vaccine Candidate Against Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis.
papers.abstract: Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis (MAP) causes Johne's disease in ruminants and is difficult to control once persistent infection is established. We designed a MAP multi-epitope vaccine candidate by screening conserved proteins and assembling predicted B-cell, MHC class I-restricted cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL), and MHC class II-restricted helper T lymphocyte (HTL) epitopes into a recombinant construct. The construct was examined by physicochemical analysis, structural modeling, molecular docking, and immune simulation, then expressed in Escherichia coli and tested in BALB/c mice as
papers.summary: The authors used immunoinformatics to design a multi-epitope vaccine against Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis (the cause of Johne's disease in ruminants), combining predicted B-cell, CTL, and HTL epitopes from conserved proteins into a single recombinant construct. They validated the design in silico (structure modeling, docking, immune simulation), expressed it in E. coli, and tested it in BALB/c mice, with macrophage transcriptomic profiling to assess immune responses. This represents a proof-of-concept candidate vaccine with preliminary immunological characterization.

papers.title: Dynamic charge distribution as a key driver of catalytic reactivity in an artificial metalloenzyme.
papers.abstract: Miniature artificial metalloenzymes provide a simplified platform to extract design principles for engineering catalysts that outperform natural enzymes. Among them, mimochromes (MCs) emerged as excellent candidates for replicating the activity of peroxidases in a compact scaffold composed of a heme center embedded between two helical peptides. However, design optimizations of MCs have largely focused on structural properties, leaving the impact of the electronic environment less explored. To investigate how the electronic environment influences reactivity, we carry out both classical and ab i
papers.summary: This study uses classical and ab initio simulations to show that dynamic charge distribution around the heme center, rather than static structural features alone, drives catalytic reactivity in mimochromes—miniature artificial metalloenzymes that mimic peroxidase activity. The work suggests that engineering the electronic environment should be a design principle for improving artificial catalysts.

papers.title: Proprietary Cationic Lipo-Oligopeptides Inhibit Herpes Simplex Virus-1 Infection.
papers.abstract: The use of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) to combat herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) infection has surged amidst the rise of HSV-1 drug-resistant strains. AMPs offer an unconventional approach to combat HSV-1 infection by exerting their activity on multiple phases of the viral life cycle, while exhibiting low rates of resistance emergence. In this study, an integrated in silico and in vitro approach was used to evaluate six proprietary cationic lipo-oligopeptides (CLOPs) (P226, P359, P577, P581, OB1105, and OB1111) as potential anti-HSV-1 agents. Computational tools were used to predict vari
papers.summary: This study evaluated six proprietary cationic lipo-oligopeptides (CLOPs) as potential anti-HSV-1 agents using an integrated in silico and in vitro approach. Computational tools were used to predict peptide properties, and the compounds were then tested experimentally for antiviral activity against herpes simplex virus type 1. The work aims to identify peptide-based alternatives to conventional antivirals amid rising HSV-1 drug resistance.

papers.title: Liposome-Supplemented Cell-free Synthesis of a Peptide that Forms β-barrel Nanopores.
papers.abstract: Rational design of nanopore-forming proteins and peptides is a promising approach for single-molecule analysis by using custom-designed nanopores tailored to specific target molecules. One challenge in this approach is the expression or synthesis of the designed nanopores, due to their high hydrophobicity. We sought to streamline the synthesis of an artificial and highly aggregative nanopore-forming peptide using liposome-supplemented cell-free protein synthesis. By optimizing the liposomal lipid composition, we recovered yields of the expressed aggregative peptide that were suitable for funct
papers.summary: The authors developed a method to synthesize a highly hydrophobic, aggregation-prone artificial peptide that forms β-barrel nanopores by supplementing cell-free protein synthesis with liposomes. Optimizing the lipid composition improved yields enough to produce functional nanopores. This streamlines the production of custom-designed nanopores for single-molecule sensing applications.

papers.title: A Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD) pipeline via DRUG-GAN: A multiscale method for drug-like/target-specific compound library generation.
papers.abstract: We present the Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a deep learning-driven pipeline for efficient drug lead identification. FSGLD integrates generative modeling with molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, ligand-residue interaction profile, MM-PBSA, thermodynamic integration (TI), and experimental validation to bridge theoretical design and practical application. The core multiscale DRUG-GAN models enable generative model-guided discovery of drug-like and target-specific compounds across three scenarios: (i) generation of random drug-like compounds, (ii) generation of t
papers.summary: The authors present FSGLD, a deep learning pipeline that combines a generative adversarial network (DRUG-GAN) with docking, molecular dynamics, MM-PBSA, thermodynamic integration, and experimental validation to design drug-like and target-specific compounds. The multiscale approach aims to bridge computational generation with practical lead discovery across multiple design scenarios.

papers.title: Substrate recognition and stage-dependent transformation of aflatoxin B1 by mediator-free Bacillus laccase frL103.
papers.abstract: Enzyme-based mitigation of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is commonly evaluated by parent-toxin depletion. This study characterized the stage-dependent, mediator-free transformation of AFB1 by recombinant Bacillus laccase frL103 and assessed chemical, biological, and structural outcomes. UHPLC-HRMS profiling at 0, 30, and 60 h yielded 2846 filtered features and showed that the AFB1 response decreased to 23.8% and 14.8% of the initial value at 30 and 60 h, respectively. A feature at m/z 329.0660 increased at 30 h and declined to 17.7% of that response at 60 h; accurate mass and MS/MS fragmentation support
papers.summary: This study characterized how a recombinant Bacillus laccase (frL103) degrades aflatoxin B1 without requiring a mediator, tracking the reaction over 60 hours. Using UHPLC-HRMS profiling, the authors found that AFB1 levels dropped to 23.8% and 14.8% of initial values at 30 and 60 hours, respectively, while a transient intermediate feature at m/z 329.0660 peaked at 30 hours before declining. The work highlights that parent-toxin depletion alone is insufficient to assess detoxification, since intermediate transformation products appear and persist in a stage-dependent manner.

papers.title: Mapping Functional Transitions across Protein Homologues from a Single Simulation: Application of gEDES-HM to Adenylate Kinases.
papers.abstract: Proteins fluctuate across different conformational states, which constitute a dynamic ensemble that regulates their interaction networks and functions. Predicting the conformational landscape remains a computational challenge, and even more difficult is capturing the link between state distributions and specific functions within protein homologues. Here, we present gEDES-HM (generalized Ensemble Docking with Enhanced sampling of pocket Shape-Homology Modeling), a scalable computational protocol enabling us to remap conformational ensembles obtained from enhanced sampling simulations of a singl
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors introduce gEDES-HM, a computational protocol that takes the conformational ensemble from an enhanced-sampling simulation of one protein and remaps it onto homologous proteins, allowing functional transitions to be predicted across a protein family from a single simulation. They demonstrate the approach on adenylate kinases, showing that state distributions can be linked to function across homologues. This offers a scalable way to study conformational landscapes and function without running expensive simulations for every family member.

papers.title: Molecular insights into GPR55 modulation reveal an atypical activation mechanism and glycosylation-dependent efficacy regulation.
papers.abstract: GPR55 is a lipid-activated G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) implicated in metabolism, inflammation, and neurodegeneration. Lysophosphatidylinositol (LPI) species are proposed as endogenous agonists, but progress in understanding GPR55 function has still been limited by suboptimal chemical probes. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of GPR55 in both inactive and active states. The inactive-state structure bound to the inverse agonist CID16020046 facilitated the rational design of an improved in vitro tool compound, BI-8310. Surprisingly, mutation of a glycosylation s
papers.summary: The authors solved cryo-EM structures of the lipid receptor GPR55 in inactive and active states, revealing an atypical activation mechanism. The inactive-state structure enabled rational design of an improved tool compound (BI-8310), and they unexpectedly found that receptor glycosylation regulates signaling efficacy. This provides a structural and pharmacological foundation for better probes to study GPR55 in metabolism, inflammation, and neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Biochemistry of protozoan Metacaspases: Structure, processing, and inhibition.
papers.abstract: Metacaspases are calcium-dependent cysteine proteases (clan CD, family C14) present in fungi, protozoa, and plants but absent from mammals. Although structurally related to metazoan caspases, they differ in substrate specificity (cleaving after arginine or lysine), calcium-dependent activation, and monomeric architecture. In protozoan parasites such as Trypanosoma brucei, T. cruzi, Leishmania spp., Plasmodium spp., and Toxoplasma gondii, metacaspases regulate programmed cell death, cell cycle progression, protein quality control, differentiation, and virulence. Their absence in humans and esse
papers.summary: This review examines metacaspases, calcium-dependent cysteine proteases found in fungi, protozoa, and plants but absent in mammals, focusing on their structure, activation processing, and inhibition. In protozoan parasites like Trypanosoma, Leishmania, Plasmodium, and Toxoplasma, these enzymes regulate programmed cell death, cell cycle progression, protein quality control, differentiation, and virulence. Because humans lack metacaspases, the review highlights their potential as selective antiparasitic drug targets.

papers.title: Structure-guided development of G protein-biased apelin receptor agonists for cardiovascular disease.
papers.abstract: Apelin receptor (APLNR) is a crucial G protein-coupled receptor that plays a central role in cardiovascular homeostasis; therefore, it represents a promising therapeutic target for heart failure, myocardial infarction, cardiac hypertrophy, and pulmonary arterial hypertension. However, the activation of APLNR simultaneously engages inhibitory G protein (Gi)-mediated protective signaling and β-arrestin pathways that are associated with pathological cardiac remodeling, thereby imposing significant limitations and challenges for the therapeutic development of conventional balanced agonists. Recent
papers.journal: Journal of Zhejiang University. Science. B
papers.summary: This paper describes the structure-guided design of apelin receptor (APLNR) agonists that preferentially activate protective G protein signaling while avoiding β-arrestin pathways linked to pathological cardiac remodeling. Such G protein-biased agonists are proposed as a strategy to improve therapeutic outcomes for heart failure, myocardial infarction, and related cardiovascular diseases.

papers.title: RAF isoform selectivity of MEK inhibitors and rational design of a covalent ARAF-MEK inhibitor.
papers.abstract: Aberrant activation of the RAS/RAF/mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK)/extracellular signal-regulated kinase pathway is a frequent cause of cancer. Allosteric MEK inhibitors block this pathway by binding RAF-MEK complexes to prevent activation of MEK by RAF. However, how MEK inhibitor potency varies across the three RAF isoforms remains poorly understood. We profiled seven allosteric MEK inhibitors and observed a notable hierarchy of sensitivity: All most potently inhibited CRAF-driven MEK activation while relatively sparing ARAF-driven activation. We identified point mutations in AR
papers.summary: This study profiles seven allosteric MEK inhibitors and finds a consistent sensitivity hierarchy across RAF isoforms, with CRAF-driven MEK activation most potently inhibited and ARAF-driven activation relatively spared. Using point mutations in ARAF, the authors map the structural basis of this isoform selectivity and then rationally design a covalent ARAF-MEK inhibitor to overcome the ARAF-sparing gap.

papers.title: How Many Crystal Structures Do You Need to Trust Your Docking Results?
papers.abstract: Structure-based drug discovery relies on the prediction of protein-bound poses of new molecule designs, the accuracy of which can impact downstream prioritization. While it is expected that crystal structures of similar molecules would provide the best template for predicting the poses of new designs, the time and cost required motivates identifying a point of diminishing returns for collecting new structures. Using 403 crystal structures of SARS-CoV-2 main protease from the open science COVID Moonshot project, we explore the tradeoff between the cost and utility of obtaining crystal structure
papers.summary: This study uses 403 crystal structures of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease from the COVID Moonshot project to determine how many experimental structures are needed before docking predictions stop improving. It finds a point of diminishing returns, offering guidance on when additional crystal structures no longer meaningfully improve pose prediction accuracy for new molecule designs.

papers.title: Evolution-Informed Viroinformatics Identifies Conserved Immune Targets with Predicted Lower Mutational Vulnerability Across Betacoronaviruses.
papers.abstract: The extensive evolutionary diversity and continuous mutational adaptation of betacoronaviruses represent a major challenge to the development of broadly protective countermeasures. This study applied an evolution-informed Viroinformatics framework to systematically identify conserved and immune targets with predicted lower mutational vulnerability across betacoronaviruses. The workflow integrated comparative sequence conservation and phylogenetic analysis with immunoinformatics-based epitope screening, HLA population coverage, mutational escape profiling, structural modeling, molecular docking
papers.summary: This study applies an evolution-informed bioinformatics pipeline to identify conserved immune targets across betacoronaviruses that are predicted to be less vulnerable to mutation. By combining sequence conservation, phylogenetics, epitope screening, HLA coverage, mutational escape profiling, and structural modeling, the authors highlight candidate targets for broadly protective countermeasures. The work is computational and predictive, offering a framework for prioritizing conserved epitopes rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Metabolic Profiling, Antioxidant Activity, and Mechanistic Insights of Chicory from Northern and Southern China: Integrating Metabolomics, Machine Learning, Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics Simulations, and In Vitro Assays.
papers.abstract: Chicory is a traditional food-medicinal plant, and its antioxidant efficacy has been recognized. However, the specific differences in the metabolic characteristics and antioxidant activity of chicory caused by geographical differences remain unclear. In this study, a total of 64 volatile components and 35 non-volatile components of northern and southern chicory were identified. Chemometric combined with machine learning was applied to screen 8 volatile and 7 non-volatile potential chemical biomarkers. Furthermore, the core targets of the chicory antioxidant were revealed by network pharmacolog
papers.summary: This study compared the metabolic profiles and antioxidant activity of chicory from northern and southern China, identifying 64 volatile and 35 non-volatile components. Using chemometrics and machine learning, the authors pinpointed 8 volatile and 7 non-volatile biomarkers that distinguish geographic origin, and combined network pharmacology, molecular docking, and dynamics simulations with in vitro assays to propose core antioxidant targets. The work links regional metabolic variation to antioxidant mechanisms, though the findings are specific to chicory and require broader validation.

papers.title: Prunus mume Extract Cooperates with Cisplatin to Induce Melanoma Apoptosis and Regulate Immune Responses.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the potential of Prunus mume (P. mume) extract as an anticancer adjuvant by evaluating its direct apoptotic effects on A375P human melanoma cells and its immunomodulatory impact on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). Furthermore, the extract demonstrated additive and chemosensitizing effects when combined with a sub-toxic dose of cisplatin, significantly enhancing the growth inhibition of A375P cells. Selective growth inhibition was confirmed using crystal violet assays, where the 80% ethanol (EtOH) extract exhibited significant dose-dependent inhibition of A375
papers.summary: This study shows that an 80% ethanol extract of Prunus mume (Chinese plum) can directly induce apoptosis in A375P melanoma cells and modulate immune responses in peripheral blood mononuclear cells. When combined with a low, sub-toxic dose of cisplatin, the extract produced additive and chemosensitizing effects, enhancing melanoma growth inhibition. The findings suggest P. mume extract may serve as a natural anticancer adjuvant, though the work is limited to in vitro cell assays.

papers.title: Design, Synthesis, Evaluation, and Molecular Dynamics Simulation of Tadalafil Derivatives for the Treatment of Erectile Dysfunction.
papers.abstract: Erectile dysfunction (ED) remains a global health burden, yet the clinical utility of tadalafil is constrained by its poor aqueous solubility, cross-inhibition of homologous PDE isoforms, and an efficacy ceiling that cannot be overcome by dose adjustment alone. Herein, a series of diketopiperazine-based tadalafil analogues were designed and synthesized by decorating the amide nitrogen with flexible carbon chains and polar fragments (glycine, taurine, cysteine, and succinic/glutaric anhydride spacers), and by replacing the 3,4-methylenedioxybenzyl motif with substituted aromatic aldehydes. All
papers.summary: The authors designed and synthesized a series of tadalafil analogues by modifying the amide nitrogen with flexible carbon chains and polar fragments and replacing the methylenedioxybenzyl group, aiming to overcome tadalafil's poor solubility and PDE isoform cross-inhibition. They evaluated the compounds and used molecular dynamics simulations to assess binding. The work is a medicinal chemistry optimization effort targeting erectile dysfunction.

papers.title: In Silico Investigation of Candidate Anticancer Targets for Aryltetralin Lignans Previously Reported from Cleistanthus Species.
papers.abstract: Aryltetralin lignans isolated from the fruits of Cleistanthus species exhibit substantial cytotoxic activity, although the molecular interactions underlying these effects remain incompletely understood. This study combined computational target investigation with previously published experimental chemical characterization and cytotoxic evidence and no new isolation or cytotoxicity experiments were carried out. Cleistantoxin, 7-hydroxypicropolygamain, neo-cleistantoxin, cleisindoside A, cleisindoside D, and cleistonkinin D were previously isolated from C. indochinensis, C. tonkinensis, C. eberha
papers.summary: This study used computational docking and target-prediction methods to investigate which proteins might mediate the anticancer effects of six aryltetralin lignans previously isolated from Cleistanthus plants. No new experiments were performed; the work integrates prior chemical and cytotoxicity data with in silico target identification. The findings propose candidate molecular targets that could guide future experimental validation of these cytotoxic natural products.

papers.title: Novel Benzimidazol-2-Acetamide Derivatives as Submicromolar Casein Kinase 1δ Inhibitors with Favourable Predicted Drug-like Properties.
papers.abstract: Background/Objective: Casein kinase 1δ (CK1δ) plays a central role in regulating circadian rhythms, DNA repair, apoptosis, and cell proliferation, and its dysregulation is associated with both cancer and neurodegenerative diseases, making CK1δ an attractive therapeutic target. This study aimed to develop novel CK1δ inhibitors with favourable drug-like properties through the synthesis and biological evaluation of benzimidazol-2-acetamide derivatives. Methods: A novel series of benzimidazol-2-acetamide derivatives was synthesized, incorporating different substituents on the benzimidazole core (5
papers.summary: This study reports the synthesis and biological evaluation of a new series of benzimidazol-2-acetamide derivatives designed as inhibitors of casein kinase 1δ (CK1δ), a target implicated in cancer and neurodegenerative disease. Several compounds achieved submicromolar potency against CK1δ and were predicted to have favourable drug-like properties, suggesting promise as starting points for further optimization.

papers.title: Computational Assessment of CKP-25 Binding at Receptor-Recognition Interfaces Across Diverse Human Coronaviruses.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The continued emergence of novel coronaviruses motivates the search for small molecules that bind conserved features of the spike receptor-recognition interface across diverse species. CKP-25 was recently reported as a small-molecule inhibitor of the SARS-CoV-2 spike receptor-binding domain. This study aimed to assess computationally whether CKP-25 can maintain stable binding at receptor-recognition interfaces across phylogenetically diverse human coronaviruses. Methods: CKP-25 was docked to the spike receptor-binding regions of Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavir
papers.summary: This computational study docked the small molecule CKP-25 against the spike receptor-binding regions of multiple human coronaviruses, including MERS-CoV, to test whether it can bind conserved features of the receptor-recognition interface across phylogenetically diverse species. The work extends prior reports of CKP-25 as a SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD inhibitor by assessing cross-species binding stability in silico. Findings are based on docking simulations rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Thermophysically Guided Design of Spray-Dried Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Microcapsules with Improved Thermal Stability.
papers.abstract: Spray drying and gastrointestinal transit can cause substantial losses in probiotic viability, limiting effective delivery in food applications. This study developed a thermophysically guided framework for the rational design of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum microcapsules in three sequential stages. First, Kissinger kinetic analysis of eleven biopolymer candidates (Ea: 95.4-198.4 kJ/mol) combined with pH-dependent solubility profiling provided an empirical screening criterion for the preselection of coating materials; the activation energies are apparent values associated with a composite endo
papers.summary: This study presents a three-stage, thermophysically guided framework for designing spray-dried Lactiplantibacillus plantarum microcapsules with improved thermal stability. Using Kissinger kinetic analysis of eleven biopolymer candidates (activation energies 95.4–198.4 kJ/mol) combined with pH-dependent solubility profiling, the authors established an empirical screening criterion for preselection of coating materials. The approach aims to reduce viability losses during spray drying and gastrointestinal transit for probiotic food delivery.

papers.title: Comparative Phytochemical and Biological Evaluation of Walnut Septum and Pellicle Extracts in Chemical, Computational, and Cell-Based Models.
papers.abstract: Background: Walnut (Juglans regia L.) processing generates polyphenol-rich by-products, including the septum (WS) and pellicle (WP). This study comparatively characterized the phytochemical composition of WS and WP from Romania and investigated their antioxidant and preliminary immunomodulatory properties using chemical, computational, and cell-based approaches. Methods: Extracts were characterized by targeted LC-QTOF-MS/MS, and antioxidant capacity was evaluated using ABTS, DPPH, and FRAP assays. Major phenolic compounds were docked against Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (KEAP1), followe
papers.summary: This study compared the polyphenol composition and bioactivity of two walnut by-products, the septum and pellicle, using LC-MS/MS profiling, chemical antioxidant assays, molecular docking against KEAP1, and cell-based immunomodulation tests. The extracts were polyphenol-rich and showed antioxidant activity, with docking suggesting KEAP1 as a possible target. The work is largely descriptive and preliminary, characterizing underutilized walnut processing waste rather than establishing new biology.

papers.title: Niosomal Mexiletine Attenuates Rotenone-Induced Parkinsonism via Modulation of the circDLGAP4/miR-134-5p/p-CREB Axis and Restoration of Mitochondrial-Autophagic Homeostasis.
papers.abstract: Background: Parkinson's disease (PD) is distinguished by progressive dopaminergic degeneration driven by the convergence of oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired autophagy. Mexiletine (Mexil), which has demonstrated antioxidant properties, has not been systematically investigated yet for its potential to mitigate mitochondrial-dysfunction-related neurodegeneration in PD. Using an integrated computational and experimental approach, we characterized, for the first time, the neuroprotective mechanisms of Mexil's action against rotenone (Rot)-induced Parkinso
papers.summary: This study shows that a niosomal formulation of the drug mexiletine protects against rotenone-induced Parkinsonism in a model system by modulating the circDLGAP4/miR-134-5p/p-CREB signaling axis and restoring mitochondrial-autophagic balance. The work combines computational and experimental approaches to characterize a novel neuroprotective mechanism for mexiletine, repurposed here for Parkinson's disease.

papers.title: Adhesives Inspired by Marine Organisms: Multifunctional Design and Application for Complex Wet/Underwater Environments.
papers.abstract: Achieving strong adhesion in humid or underwater environments is a long-term challenge in materials science. Water molecules form a hydration layer on the substrate surface, blocking effective contact between the adhesive and the interface, leading to the failure of traditional adhesives. The wet adhesion strength of viscoelastic materials is due to the synergistic effect of interfacial chemical bonds and multiscale energy dissipation, but water environment can seriously interfere with this mechanism. In nature, mussels, barnacles, and sandcastle worms have evolved unique wet adhesion strategi
papers.summary: This review surveys how marine organisms such as mussels, barnacles, and sandcastle worms achieve strong adhesion in wet and underwater conditions, and how these biological strategies inspire synthetic adhesive design. It emphasizes that wet adhesion depends on the synergy between interfacial chemical bonding and multiscale energy dissipation, and discusses how water's hydration layer disrupts this mechanism in conventional adhesives. The paper consolidates design principles for multifunctional adhesives targeting complex humid and underwater environments.

papers.title: Butein Interacts at the Minor Groove of DNA: Multi-Spectroscopic, Thermodynamic, and Bioinformatic Analyses.
papers.abstract: DNA is an important therapeutic target, and characterizing its interactions with small molecules can inform drug development. Butein is a chalcone with reported antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer activities. This study investigated the interaction between butein and calf thymus DNA using spectroscopic and computational methods. UV-visible absorption and fluorescence quenching measurements supported complex formation. Fluorescence-derived binding constants ranged from 4.04 × 103 to 5.62 × 103 M-1, indicating weak to moderate binding affinity. Thermodynamic analysis indicated spontan
papers.summary: This study characterizes how the plant-derived compound butein binds to calf thymus DNA using spectroscopy, thermodynamics, and computational docking. The results indicate weak-to-moderate binding affinity (K ~10^3–10^4 M⁻¹) with butein interacting at the DNA minor groove, and the binding is thermodynamically spontaneous. This provides a mechanistic basis for butein's reported biological activities and its potential as a DNA-targeting therapeutic scaffold.

papers.title: A Pathway-Driven Computational Drug Discovery Framework Integrating Machine Learning and Virtual Screening for Identification of Anti-Rheumatoid Arthritis Natural Small Molecules.
papers.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to establish a pathway-driven computational drug discovery framework integrating machine learning, target prioritization, virtual screening, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and in vitro evaluation to identify natural small molecules with potential anti-rheumatoid arthritis (RA) activity. Methods: Sixteen RA-related Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets were included, with 15 cohorts used for model development and one reserved for independent external validation. Pathway features quantified by gene set variation analysis (GSVA) were subjected to cohort-aware fe
papers.summary: The authors built a computational pipeline that combines pathway-level features from 16 rheumatoid arthritis GEO datasets with machine learning, target prioritization, virtual screening, and molecular dynamics to identify natural small molecules with potential anti-RA activity, followed by in vitro validation. The framework is pathway-driven rather than single-gene-driven, aiming to improve robustness of candidate selection. This is a methodological integration study with a disease-specific application.

papers.title: Microbial Rhodopsins: Structural-Functional Mechanisms and the Design of Optogenetic Silencing Tools-With Emphasis on Halorubrum Archaeorhodopsins.
papers.abstract: Microbial rhodopsins are light-sensitive membrane proteins that use retinal as a covalent chromophore and adopt a seven-transmembrane α-helical fold. They are widely distributed across archaea, bacteria, algae, and fungi and mediate diverse functions, including light-driven ion transport, light-gated ion conduction, and photosensory signaling. Since the discovery of bacteriorhodopsin in 1971, the microbial rhodopsin family has expanded continuously, and channelrhodopsin-based optogenetics has revolutionized neuroscience by enabling millisecond-scale optical control of neuronal activity. Howeve
papers.summary: This review examines the structural and functional mechanisms of microbial rhodopsins—seven-transmembrane retinal-binding proteins found across archaea, bacteria, algae, and fungi—that mediate light-driven ion transport, light-gated conduction, and photosensory signaling. It emphasizes halorubrum archaeorhodopsins and discusses how mechanistic understanding informs the design of optogenetic silencing tools, building on the channelrhodopsin-based optogenetics revolution in neuroscience.

papers.title: Rational Design of Molecularly Imprinted Nanozymes for Selective Degradation of Poly(bisphenol A carbonate) (BPA-PC).
papers.abstract: Poly(bisphenol A carbonate) (BPA-PC) is an engineering thermoplastic whose recycling is hindered by its Code-7 classification and environmental BPA leaching. Here, we report water-soluble molecularly imprinted nanozymes for the selective depolymerization of BPA-PC under mild alkaline conditions. Synthesized within cross-linked surfactant micelles, the optimized nanozyme combines shape-complementary BPA-matched pockets with surface basicity, achieving a 72-fold rate enhancement over porcine pancreatic lipase. Fluorescence titrations with a soluble dansyl-labeled BPA-PC dimer confirm strong subs
papers.summary: The authors designed water-soluble molecularly imprinted nanozymes that selectively depolymerize poly(bisphenol A carbonate) under mild alkaline conditions. The optimized nanozyme combines BPA-shaped binding pockets with surface basicity, achieving a 72-fold rate enhancement over porcine pancreatic lipase. This offers a promising approach to recycling a problematic plastic while reducing BPA leaching.

papers.title: Rationally Designed Phenyl- and Phenanthryl-Based Imidazole Hybrids for the Treatment of Breast Cancer-A Structure-Activity Relationship Study.
papers.abstract: A series of 11 compounds of phenyl-imidazole-pyrrole and 9 compounds of phenanthryl-imidazole-pyrrole were synthesized and evaluated against breast cancer cell lines differing in the expression of estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR) and human epidermal growth factor receptor (HER)-2, viz., BT-474 (ER+, PR+, and HER2+), T-47D and MCF-7 (ER+, PR+, and HER2-), and MDA-MB-468 and MDA-MB-231 (ER-, PR-, and HER2-). The analysis of the results indicated that the most active compounds were 5d and 5k from the phenyl-imidazole-pyrrole series and 6b and 6i from the phenanthryl-imidazole-py
papers.summary: The authors synthesized and tested 20 new phenyl- and phenanthryl-imidazole-pyrrole hybrid compounds against five breast cancer cell lines with different receptor statuses (ER/PR/HER2). Several compounds (5d, 5k, 6b, 6i) showed notable activity, and the structure-activity relationships suggest that the phenanthryl-based scaffold may offer improved potency. This is an early-stage medicinal chemistry study identifying lead compounds for further optimization.

papers.title: Targeting FTSJ1 to Restore TP53 Function in Nonsense Mutation-Driven Cancer: Computational and Experimental Evaluation of 1,2,4-Triazole Derivatives.
papers.abstract: Nonsense mutations introduce premature termination codons (PTCs) into mRNA transcripts, leading to truncated and non-functional proteins, and accounting for approximately 10-15% of genetic disorders. In this context, the induction of translational readthrough by small molecules, known as translational readthrough-inducing drugs (TRIDs), has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy to restore full-length protein expression. However, the mechanism of action of TRIDs is still under debate, and one emerging target is FTSJ1, a methyltransferase involved in tRNA modification. FTSJ1 regulates tran
papers.summary: This study investigates 1,2,4-triazole derivatives as translational readthrough-inducing drugs (TRIDs) that target the FTSJ1 methyltransferase to restore full-length TP53 protein in cancers driven by nonsense mutations. Using computational screening combined with experimental validation, the authors propose FTSJ1 as a druggable node for suppressing premature termination codons and reactivating tumor suppressor function. The work offers a proof-of-concept for small-molecule readthrough therapy in nonsense-mutation cancers.

papers.title: Pyridine-3-Carboxamide-1,3,4-Thiadiazole Hybrids as Antimicrobial Agents: Synthesis, Biological Evaluation, In Vivo Toxicity, and Computational Studies.
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of antimicrobial resistance necessitates the development of novel antimicrobial agents with improved efficacy and favorable safety profiles. In this study, a new series of pyridine-3-carboxamide-1,3,4-thiadiazole hybrids and their corresponding N-Mannich bases bearing structurally diverse piperazine substituents were designed, synthesized, and characterized by FT-IR, 1H/13C NMR, and HR-MS. Their antimicrobial activity was evaluated against reference and clinical bacterial and fungal strains using broth microdilution and agar diffusion assays. The compounds exhibited selecti
papers.summary: This study designed and synthesized a new series of pyridine-3-carboxamide-1,3,4-thiadiazole hybrids and their N-Mannich base derivatives with piperazine substituents, then tested them against bacterial and fungal strains. The compounds showed selective antimicrobial activity, and the authors also assessed in vivo toxicity and performed computational studies to support the findings. The work aims to address antimicrobial resistance by identifying new drug candidates with favorable safety profiles.

papers.title: Targeted LC-MS/MS Phytochemical Profiling and Synergistic Anti-Urease Activity of Limoniastrum guyonianum Extracts Supported by Molecular Docking and In Silico ADME and Drug-Likeness Assessment.
papers.abstract: Limoniastrum guyonianum Durieu ex Boiss. is an endemic halophyte native to the semi-arid regions of North Africa and represents an under-explored source of bioactive phytochemicals. This study investigated the phytochemical composition and anti-urease potential of L. guyonianum aerial parts through an integrated experimental and computational approach. Plant material was subjected to sequential organic extraction and an additional independent aqueous extract was prepared from the raw plant; the resulting organic fractions were characterized using a targeted LC-MS/MS method validated for 53 phy
papers.summary: This study profiled the phytochemical composition of the North African halophyte Limoniastrum guyonianum using targeted LC-MS/MS and tested its extracts for anti-urease activity, finding synergistic inhibition supported by molecular docking and in silico ADME/drug-likeness analyses. The work positions this under-explored plant as a source of bioactive compounds with potential urease-inhibitory applications.

papers.title: Exploratory In Silico Evaluation of Microencapsulation Matrices for Indomethacin.
papers.abstract: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), such as indomethacin (ID), may produce gastrointestinal adverse effects associated with cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1) inhibition, motivating the investigation of microencapsulation strategies for modulating drug release. However, protein-based encapsulating materials remain comparatively underexplored using molecular simulation relative to synthetic polymers. In this study, the interaction tendencies of ID with cottonseed flour protein (CFP) and maltodextrin (MD) as potential encapsulating matrices were explored in silico using molecular dynamics simul
papers.summary: This study used molecular dynamics simulations to explore how indomethacin interacts with two potential microencapsulation materials: cottonseed flour protein and maltodextrin. The goal was to assess whether these matrices could modulate drug release and reduce gastrointestinal side effects associated with NSAIDs. The work is exploratory and computational, providing preliminary insight into protein-based encapsulation design.

papers.title: From whole-exome sequencing to functional insight: Characterization of rare germline variants in lung cancer.
papers.abstract: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) has greatly expanded the identification of rare germline variants in hereditary cancer predisposition. However, the interpretation of variants of uncertain significance (VUS), particularly in novel candidate genes, remains a major challenge in lung cancer genetics.
papers.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of interpreting rare germline variants of uncertain significance (VUS) identified through whole-exome sequencing in lung cancer predisposition. It moves beyond variant discovery toward functional characterization of candidate variants in novel genes, aiming to distinguish pathogenic from benign variants. The work highlights the gap between WES-based variant identification and actionable clinical interpretation in lung cancer genetics.

papers.title: Designing Cooperative Molecular Glues for FKBP12-MAPRE1 with Enhanced-Sampling Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: Molecular glues (MGs) offer a unique modality for inducing protein-protein interactions (PPIs), yet their rational design is often hindered by the limitations of static structural data. Here, we present a computational pipeline for the design of cooperative MGs for the FKBP12-MAPRE1 system using replica exchange with solute scaling (REST2) for enhanced sampling in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. By sampling the conformational ensembles of binary and ternary complexes, we identified a "stabilized configurational space" that facilitates ternary-complex formation through a combination of con
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational pipeline for designing molecular glues that induce protein-protein interactions between FKBP12 and MAPRE1, using enhanced-sampling molecular dynamics (REST2) to explore conformational ensembles of binary and ternary complexes. The authors identify a 'stabilized configurational space' that promotes ternary-complex formation through cooperative binding effects, moving beyond static structural data for rational glue design.

papers.title: Dietary Curcumin Protects Common Carp (Cyprinus carpio) Against Potassium Permanganate-Induced Toxicity: Hematological, Immunological, Oxidative, and Molecular Docking Evidence.
papers.abstract: Potassium permanganate treatment can adversely affect fish physiology despite its usefulness in aquaculture. This study evaluated the protective effects of dietary curcumin against potassium permanganate-induced disturbances in common carp (Cyprinus carpio). Fish were fed a basal diet or diets supplemented with 1%, 2%, or 4% curcumin for eight weeks, with or without subsequent exposure to potassium permanganate at 2 mg/L for 30 min daily for seven days. Hematological and immune parameters and oxidative status in the liver, kidney, spleen, and gill were assessed. Potassium permanganate exposure
papers.summary: This study shows that feeding common carp a curcumin-supplemented diet (1–4%) for eight weeks reduces the hematological, immunological, and oxidative damage caused by potassium permanganate exposure. Molecular docking evidence is also presented to support curcumin's protective mechanism. The work suggests dietary curcumin could be a practical protective strategy in aquaculture where potassium permanganate is used as a treatment.

papers.title: Exploring the Underlying Molecular Mechanisms of Chaetomugilin Q in Breast Cancer Using Network Pharmacology, Molecular Docking, and Bioinformatics.
papers.abstract: Chaetomugilin Q has demonstrated anti-tumor effects in preclinical models. However, the potential mechanisms of chaetomugilin Q in treating breast cancer remain unclear. This study used network pharmacology and molecular docking prediction to explore these mechanisms and prioritize candidate targets of chaetomugilin Q in breast cancer. PharmMapper, SuperPred, and GalaxySagittarius-AF were utilized to obtain targets associated with chaetomugilin Q, while GeneCards, CTD, DrugBank, OMIM, and TTD were used to collect breast cancer-related targets. A total of 299 overlapping candidate targets were
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology, molecular docking, and bioinformatics to predict how the natural compound chaetomugilin Q might act against breast cancer. The authors identified 299 candidate target proteins shared between the compound and breast cancer, then prioritized them through docking and pathway analysis. The work is purely computational and provides hypotheses for future experimental validation rather than direct evidence of efficacy.

papers.title: Research on the Intervention of Bile Stasis-Induced Pruritus Using Small Molecules Targeting MRGPRX4 Through High-Throughput Screening.
papers.abstract: MRGPRX4, which is mainly expressed in human sensory neurons, is a key mediator of cholestatic pruritus, but clinically available small-molecule inhibitors targeting it remain very scarce; thus, this study aims to screen out novel active inhibitors targeting MRGPRX4. In this work, we performed high-throughput virtual screening of the small-molecule compound library with Schrodinger software targeting MRGPRX4, and selected the top five commercially available compounds with the highest scores from 13,144 candidate compounds. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation were used for virtua
papers.summary: This study used computational high-throughput virtual screening of over 13,000 compounds to identify small-molecule inhibitors of MRGPRX4, a receptor on sensory neurons that drives itching in cholestatic (bile stasis) liver disease. Five top-scoring commercially available compounds were selected and validated through molecular docking and dynamics simulations. The work provides candidate starting points for developing drugs to treat cholestatic pruritus, a condition with few targeted treatment options.

papers.title: LC-MS-Based Metabolomic Profiling of Excoecaria agallocha Leaf Extract: Integrated Antioxidant, Anti-Inflammatory, Cholinesterase Inhibitory and Neuroprotective Evaluation with AChE-Targeted Molecular Docking.
papers.abstract: Excoecaria agallocha L. is a medicinally important mangrove species containing diverse secondary metabolites with potential antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neuroprotective activities. This study investigated the multifunctional biological potential of E. agallocha leaves using petroleum ether, chloroform, ethyl acetate, methanol, and aqueous extracts. Preliminary phytochemical screening revealed a solvent-dependent distribution of constituents, while total phenolic and flavonoid contents were quantified in the methanolic and aqueous extracts. Antioxidant activity was evaluated using DPPH r
papers.summary: This study profiled the leaf extract of the mangrove Excoecaria agallocha using LC-MS metabolomics and tested its extracts for antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, cholinesterase-inhibitory, and neuroprotective activities. Methanolic and aqueous extracts were richest in phenolics and flavonoids, and molecular docking suggested AChE as a target for the detected compounds. The work is a preliminary in vitro and in silico characterization of a medicinal plant, without in vivo validation.

papers.title: GDEE: A Structure-Based Platform for Gene Discovery and Enzyme Engineering.
papers.abstract: Enzymes are extensively utilized for catalyzing the production of value-added compounds in diverse sectors with significant economic impact. However, challenges such as poor protein expression, low catalytic activity, substrate/co-factor limitations, and toxicity of final products limit the efficiency of these biocatalysts. Protein engineering offers a solution by redesigning enzyme catalytic properties to enhance biosynthetic pathways. In this study, we present an automated platform for gene discovery and enzyme engineering, aimed at overcoming these bottlenecks. The GDEE platform finds and o
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: GDEE is an automated computational platform that integrates structure-based methods to discover genes and engineer enzymes, addressing common biocatalyst limitations like poor expression, low activity, and substrate/co-factor constraints. It aims to streamline the redesign of enzyme catalytic properties to improve biosynthetic pathways.

papers.title: 2-Aminoisobutylic Acid-Stabilized Helical Peptides for Selective Mitochondrial Gene Delivery.
papers.abstract: Efficient gene delivery to mitochondria remains a major challenge in the development of organelle-targeted therapeutics. Here, we report the rational design and evaluation of helix stabilized mitochondria-targeting peptides (MTPs) via the incorporation of 2-aminoisobutyric acid (Aib), a noncanonical residue known to promote helical structure and increase membrane permeability. Three essential peptides were newly synthesized by systematically substituting alanine or glycine residues with Aib in a peptide derived from the mitochondrial outer membrane protein mitoNEET. Structural analyses using m
papers.summary: This paper describes the design of helical peptides stabilized by the noncanonical residue 2-aminoisobutyric acid (Aib) to target mitochondria and deliver genetic cargo. By substituting alanine or glycine residues in a mitoNEET-derived peptide, the authors created variants with enhanced helical structure and membrane permeability, aiming to overcome the longstanding challenge of mitochondrial gene delivery. The work presents a rational peptide engineering strategy for organelle-specific therapeutics.

papers.title: A Dipeptide Module Substitution-Based Strategy for the Modification and Evaluation of ACE Inhibitory Peptides.
papers.abstract: Food-derived angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitory peptide LYPVK exhibits promising potential for application as an important ingredient with a potential antihypertensive effect in functional foods. However, the structure-activity relationship and the rational design strategy for peptide modification remain insufficiently understood. To address this, dipeptide module substitution was employed to modify and investigate the mechanism of this food-derived ACE inhibitory peptide, providing an insight into the structure-activity relationship. Through integration of molecular docking and ac
papers.summary: This study introduces a dipeptide module substitution strategy to modify the food-derived ACE inhibitory peptide LYPVK, aiming to clarify its structure-activity relationship and enable rational design. By combining molecular docking with activity assays, the authors identify key dipeptide modules that influence ACE inhibition, providing a framework for optimizing antihypertensive peptides in functional foods.

papers.title: CRISPR/Cas12a-Based Aptasensor for Cas9 Protein Detection in Spiked Food Matrices.
papers.abstract: Residual gene editors are a concern associated with the widespread application of CRISPR/Cas9 technology. Here, we developed a CRISPR/Cas12a-based fluorescent aptasensor for the qualitative and quantitative detection of Cas9 protein. Secondary structure prediction and molecular docking were combined to identify potential binding sites of the Cas9-specific aptamer. A fluorescence aptasensor was constructed based on competitive binding: in the presence of Cas9, the aptamer binds to the target and releases complementary DNA (cDNA), which activates the trans-cleavage activity of Cas12a. Cas12a sub
papers.summary: The authors developed a fluorescent aptasensor that uses a Cas9-specific aptamer and the trans-cleavage activity of Cas12a to detect residual Cas9 protein in food matrices. In the presence of Cas9, the aptamer binds the target and releases complementary DNA that activates Cas12a, producing a measurable fluorescent signal. This provides a qualitative and quantitative method for monitoring residual gene editors in food.

papers.title: MesoScreen: A Computational Platform Providing Unified Data for Liquid-Crystal Research.
papers.abstract: The development of advanced liquid-crystal (LC) materials requires reliable and standardized structure-property data, yet generating such data through molecular simulation remains time-consuming and technically demanding. Here, we present MesoScreen, an online computational platform that converts SMILES-encoded molecular structures into standardized simulation workflows. Under consistent conditions, MesoScreen generates unified multi-property profiles including molecular polarizability, orientational order and phase, density, birefringence, and a director mean-square-displacement-based estimat
papers.summary: MesoScreen is an online computational platform that takes SMILES-encoded molecular structures and runs standardized molecular simulation workflows to produce unified multi-property profiles for liquid-crystal materials, including polarizability, orientational order and phase, density, birefringence, and a director mean-square-displacement-based estimate. It addresses the lack of reliable, standardized structure-property data in liquid-crystal research by automating otherwise time-consuming and technically demanding simulations.

papers.title: Food-Derived Umami Peptides: Linking Candidate Discovery, Experimental Validation, and Food Applications.
papers.abstract: Alternative proteins and cultivated meat increase the need for flavour strategies that maintain savoury quality with less reliance on salt and conventional seasonings. Food-derived umami peptides are promising candidates, but their practical value depends on evidence beyond sequence prediction. With advances in virtual digestion, peptidomics, and AI-assisted approaches, discovery is expanding from sensory-guided preparation toward candidate-library construction and data-driven prioritization. This review compares food-protein resources and experimental and sequence-based discovery routes, and
papers.summary: This review examines food-derived umami peptides as a strategy for maintaining savory flavor in alternative proteins and cultivated meat while reducing reliance on salt and conventional seasonings. It compares food-protein resources and discovery approaches, spanning sensory-guided preparation, virtual digestion, peptidomics, and AI-assisted candidate prioritization, and emphasizes that practical value requires experimental validation beyond sequence prediction.

papers.title: C-RAF Sequence-Encoded Cooperativity Hotspots for 14-3-3/C-RAF Molecular Glues.
papers.abstract: 14-3-3 Proteins are hub proteins with an extensive interactome of phosphorylated client proteins, making them attractive targets for molecular glues (MGs) that stabilize specific 14-3-3/client protein complexes. However, selectively stabilizing individual 14-3-3 protein-protein interactions (PPIs) remains a key challenge for effectively drugging the 14-3-3 interactome. Here, we systematically investigated the sequence-encoded determinants underlying selective stabilization of the 14-3-3/C-RAF complex by covalent MGs. Using stepwise C-terminal peptide sequence extension, alanine scanning, and M
papers.summary: This study systematically dissects how the amino acid sequence of C-RAF's C-terminal region encodes selectivity for molecular glues that stabilize the 14-3-3/C-RAF protein-protein interaction. Using stepwise peptide extension and alanine scanning, the authors identify sequence-encoded cooperativity hotspots that determine selective glue activity. The work provides a framework for designing molecular glues with improved selectivity across the 14-3-3 interactome.

papers.title: A Generalized Theory for the Structural and Spatial Mapping of Energy, Entropy, and Free Energy.
papers.abstract: Systems in which the free energy density is nonuniform in space are familiar; the surface tension of a water droplet and the surface energy of a solid are good examples. Some such cases can be treated with prior theory, notably inhomogeneous solvation theory (IST), but IST is applicable only to liquids. Despite this limitation, IST has proven useful as a guide to the design of ligands to bind a targeted protein, based on the idea that ligands that displace high free energy water will tend to bind more tightly, other things being equal. Here, we present Generalized Thermodynamic Mapping (GTM) t
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
papers.summary: The authors introduce Generalized Thermodynamic Mapping (GTM), a theoretical framework that extends inhomogeneous solvation theory (IST) beyond liquids to map energy, entropy, and free energy in structurally and spatially nonuniform systems. This generalization could broaden the applicability of free-energy-based analyses, such as ligand design strategies that rely on displacing high-free-energy water, to a wider range of physical and biological contexts.

papers.title: Stoichiometry-dependent gating and structural pharmacology of cardiac GIRK1/4 channels.
papers.abstract: Cardiac G protein-gated inwardly rectifying potassium-K + (GIRK) channels, formed by GIRK1/4 heterotetramers or GIRK4 homotetramers, are crucial regulators of heart rate, and their dysfunction is associated with atrial fibrillation. Despite their therapeutic potential as anti-arrhythmic targets, development of selective GIRK modulators has been limited by an incomplete understanding of their structures, gating mechanisms, and pharmacology. Here, we report high-resolution structures of the GIRK4 homotetramer and of GIRK1/4 heterotetramers, revealing that they form in unexpected 1:3 and 2:2 asse
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint presents high-resolution cryo-EM structures of cardiac GIRK channels, revealing that GIRK1/4 heterotetramers assemble in unexpected 1:3 and 2:2 stoichiometries rather than only the assumed 2:2 arrangement. The work shows that subunit stoichiometry affects channel gating and pharmacology, providing a structural basis for developing selective anti-arrhythmic modulators targeting atrial fibrillation.

papers.title: PepRePs: Peptide-Retargeted Phosphatases Designed with Generative Language Models.
papers.abstract: Phosphorylation is a fast, reversible layer of post-translational control that directly governs protein activity, signaling flux, and cell state. Kinases and phosphatases collectively establish these phosphorylation states, but their dysregulation drives cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, and developmental disorders. Selectively manipulating the phosphorylation of individual proteins in cells remains challenging, particularly for disordered substrates. Here, we introduce Pep tide- Re targeted P hosphatase s ( PepRePs ), a genetically encoded system that fuses a peptide binder to a serine/thre
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present PepRePs, a genetically encoded system that retargets phosphatases to specific substrate proteins by fusing them to peptide binders designed with generative language models. This enables selective manipulation of phosphorylation on individual proteins in cells, including disordered substrates that are otherwise difficult to target. The approach addresses a long-standing gap in the ability to control phosphatase activity with substrate specificity.

papers.title: Functional Consequence of IRF6 Variants in Van der Woude Syndrome.
papers.abstract: Van der Woude syndrome (VWS) is the most common syndromic form of orofacial clefts (OFCs). The heritability of VWS is largely (~70%) explained by variants in the IRF6 gene. Experimental studies to confirm genetic variant effects are essential but are time intensive and expensive. Advancing next-generation sequencing techniques has made it possible to identify genetic variation quicker than their causal effects in disease processes can be ascertained. Therefore, employing computational tools to reliably predict their causal effects is crucial for advancing translational research. We conducted S
papers.summary: This study applies computational prediction tools to assess the functional consequences of IRF6 gene variants associated with Van der Woude syndrome, the most common syndromic form of orofacial clefts. Since experimental validation of variants is costly and time-consuming, the authors evaluate whether in silico methods can reliably prioritize causal variants in IRF6. The work aims to support translational research by streamlining variant interpretation for this clefting disorder.

papers.title: Application of computational methods in the drug discovery and development of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a prevalent neurodegenerative disorder marked by the accumulation of amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles in the brain, leading to cognitive decline. As the most common dementia, AD affects over 50 million individuals worldwide, with 10 million new cases each year. Despite many significant progresses in AD research fields, there is still no effective treatment. Advances in molecular modelling and artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm have facilitated the application of computational methods in AD drug development, offering advantages in terms of efficiency,
papers.summary: This review surveys how computational approaches—molecular modeling and AI algorithms—are being applied across Alzheimer's disease drug discovery and development, from target identification to lead optimization. Given the lack of effective AD treatments despite decades of research, the authors argue these in silico methods offer efficiency advantages over traditional experimental pipelines. The paper serves as an overview of the current computational toolkit available to AD drug hunters.

papers.title: Structural basis for inhibition of the lipid flippase MurJ by phage lysis protein SglPP7 suggests convergent evolution with other Sgl peptides.
papers.abstract: Some bacteriophages encode lysis proteins that inhibit essential bacterial processes, and elucidating their mechanisms is valuable for developing antibacterial strategies against drug-resistant pathogens. We determined the cryo-EM structure of the complex between the essential Escherichia coli lipid II flippase MurJ and the phage lysis protein SglPP7. Structural, mutational, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation analyses revealed that SglPP7 binds along the intramembrane cleft of MurJ and inserts its C-terminal tail into the internal cavity, stabilizing MurJ in an outward-facing conformation.
papers.summary: This study reports the cryo-EM structure of the E. coli lipid II flippase MurJ bound to the phage lysis protein SglPP7. SglPP7 binds along MurJ's intramembrane cleft and inserts its C-terminal tail into the internal cavity, locking the transporter in an outward-facing conformation. Combined mutational and MD analyses suggest this inhibition mechanism arose convergently with other Sgl peptides, highlighting phage lysis proteins as templates for antibacterial design.

papers.title: Integrative Machine Learning and Immunoinformatics-Guided Design and In Silico Validation of a Multiepitope DNA Vaccine Against Avian Metapneumovirus.
papers.abstract: Avian metapneumovirus (aMPV) is an emerging viral pathogen causing many outbreaks in chickens all over the world. There are several subtypes of the MPV circulating in chickens in the US. The current circulating subtypes of the virus in the US chicken are A, B, and C. Despite the availability of some aMPV vaccines in the US, most of these vaccines are based on foreign strains, particularly European aMPV-A/B strains. Their protective efficacy against contemporary U.S. aMPV isolates has not been fully established. The main goal of this study is to integrate the most recent aMPV genome sequencing
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning and immunoinformatics to design a multiepitope DNA vaccine against avian metapneumovirus (aMPV), targeting the A, B, and C subtypes currently circulating in U.S. chickens. The vaccine construct was validated entirely in silico, meaning no laboratory or animal testing was performed. The work addresses the gap that existing U.S. vaccines are based on older European strains with uncertain protection against current isolates.

papers.title: Antibody peptide conjugates as multifunctional therapeutics: Mechanisms, challenges, and prospects.
papers.abstract: Antibody peptide conjugates (APCs) represent a newly emerging class of targeted biotherapeutics that embody a novel structural paradigm by combining the precise targeting capabilities of antibodies with the versatile biological functions of peptides. APCs not only overcome the inherent limitations of conventional peptide therapeutics but also go beyond the cytotoxicity-focused paradigm of traditional antibody drug conjugates (ADCs). By flexibly combining peptide payload activities with antibody functions, APCs have developed into diverse therapeutic strategies, including immunomodulation, targ
papers.summary: This review introduces antibody-peptide conjugates (APCs) as an emerging class of targeted biotherapeutics that combine antibodies' precise targeting with peptides' versatile biological functions. Unlike traditional antibody-drug conjugates that focus on cytotoxicity, APCs enable diverse strategies such as immunomodulation and other mechanisms. The paper discusses the design principles, mechanisms of action, current challenges, and future prospects for this therapeutic platform.

papers.title: BD2-selective BRD4 inhibitor ZX29 mitigates myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury via BRD4-YY1-NCOA4 axis disruption and ferroptosis inhibition.
papers.abstract: Myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury (MI/RI) remains a major barrier to ischemic heart disease treatment, as reperfusion therapies often exacerbate cardiac damage. Bromodomain-containing protein 4 (BRD4) is a key epigenetic target in cardiovascular diseases, but pan-BRD4 inhibitors cause severe off-target toxicity by disrupting basal bromodomain 1 (BD1) function, highlighting the need for BD2-selective agents. This study aimed to develop a BD2-selective BRD4 inhibitor and clarify its mechanism. ZX29 was developed via virtual screening of 100,000 compounds and structure-based optimization, ex
papers.summary: The authors developed ZX29, a BD2-selective BRD4 inhibitor, through virtual screening and structure-based optimization, and showed it mitigates myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury in models. Mechanistically, ZX29 disrupts a BRD4-YY1-NCOA4 axis and inhibits ferroptosis, offering a potentially safer alternative to pan-BRD4 inhibitors that cause toxicity via BD1 disruption.

papers.title: Drugging the "undruggable" p53: a structure-guided strategy against the Y220C mutation.
papers.abstract: Tumor Protein p53 (TP53) is the most frequently altered gene in human cancer, yet mutant p53 has long been considered undruggable. The Y220C mutation is exceptional because it both destabilizes the p53 DNA-binding domain (DBD) and creates a unique surface pocket absent in wild-type protein. Availability of structural information enabled structure-based development of rezatapopt (PC14586), which binds this neo-pocket, stabilizes mutant p53, and restores transcriptional tumor suppressor activity. Early clinical studies in the PYNNACLE trial provide proof-of-concept efficacy and reveal emerging o
papers.summary: This review discusses structure-guided drug development targeting the p53 Y220C mutation, which creates a unique surface pocket not present in wild-type p53. The compound rezatapopt (PC14586) binds this neo-pocket, stabilizes the mutant protein, and restores its tumor suppressor function, with early clinical data from the PYNNACLE trial showing proof-of-concept efficacy. The work illustrates how structural biology can render a previously 'undruggable' cancer target tractable.

papers.title: Structure-Based Design and Biological Evaluation of Imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine Derivatives as Potential Antituberculosis Agents.
papers.abstract: A library of 11 novel imidazopyridine-based sulfonamide derivatives (4a-4k) were synthesized through the coupling of an imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine hydrochloride intermediate with various substituted sulfonyl chloride derivatives (3a-3k). The structures of the compounds (4a-4k) were confirmed using appropriate spectroscopic techniques. The synthesized derivatives (4a-4k) were subsequently evaluated for their antitubercular and antioxidant potential. Among the tested molecules, compounds 4b, 4d, and 4g demonstrated moderate antimycobacterial activity, displaying minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a library of 11 imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine sulfonamide derivatives and tested them for antitubercular and antioxidant activity. Three compounds (4b, 4d, 4g) showed moderate antimycobacterial activity, though the reported MIC values indicate only modest potency. The work is an early-stage medicinal chemistry exploration without structural validation of a target.

papers.title: Machine learning, molecular docking, and experimental validation identify shared molecular signatures between idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension and malignant pleural mesothelioma: a retrospective study.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH) exhibits cancer-like features, yet its pathogenesis remains unclear. Given molecular similarities between IPAH and malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM), this study aimed to uncover shared transcriptomic patterns.
papers.summary: This study used machine learning and molecular docking to identify shared transcriptomic signatures between idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH) and malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM), then validated key findings experimentally. The work suggests overlapping molecular mechanisms between the two diseases, potentially informing new therapeutic targets or repurposing opportunities.

papers.title: Unleashing the industrial potential of microbial plant cell wall polysaccharide-degrading enzymes: recent advances in protein engineering.
papers.abstract: Plant cell wall polysaccharide-degrading enzymes (PCWPEs) used in industry are predominantly of microbial origin. Key enzyme classes, including cellulases, lytic polysaccharide monooxygenases (LPMOs), β-xylanases, β-mannanases and pectinases, have attained technological maturity and are widely deployed across agro-waste biorefineries, food and feed processing, textile and pulp manufacturing. Low catalytic efficiency, insufficient thermostability, poor operational adaptability, restricted functionality, and product inhibition limit the industrial use of these enzymes. Structure- and sequence-gu
papers.summary: This review surveys recent protein engineering advances aimed at improving microbial plant cell wall polysaccharide-degrading enzymes (cellulases, LPMOs, xylanases, mannanases, pectinases) for industrial use. It focuses on overcoming limitations such as low catalytic efficiency, poor thermostability, and product inhibition through structure- and sequence-guided engineering strategies. The paper consolidates how these modifications can enhance enzyme performance across biorefining, food/feed, textile, and pulp applications.

papers.title: Tailoring plant-based food emulsions with oil bodies and proteins recovered by alkali aqueous extraction from rapeseed (Brassica napus L.) oilseeds.
papers.abstract: Oil bodies (OBs) and storage proteins recovered from oilseeds by aqueous extraction are promising ingredients for the development of plant-based food emulsions. This study aimed to co-extract natural OBs and storage proteins from rapeseed oilseeds, to explore the microstructure, to analyse the composition, to investigate the emulsifying properties of the proteins and to determine the impact of pH on the physical stability of natural OBs, homogenized OBs, proteins and protein-stabilized oil droplets in emulsions. Alkali aqueous extraction at pH 9.5 enabled the recovery of well-dispersed OBs tog
papers.summary: This study co-extracts natural oil bodies and storage proteins from rapeseed using alkaline aqueous extraction at pH 9.5, yielding well-dispersed oil bodies suitable as plant-based emulsion ingredients. The authors characterize the microstructure and composition of these extracts and examine how pH affects the physical stability of natural and homogenized oil bodies, proteins, and protein-stabilized oil droplets. The work supports using recovered oilseed components as functional ingredients for designing plant-based food emulsions.

papers.title: Exploring molecular interactions between yeast topoisomerase I and RNA polymerase III subunit, Rpc82 using an in-silico approach.
papers.abstract: The process of DNA transcription leads to the generation of torsional stress, which must be resolved for smooth progression of the transcription machinery. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, DNA topoisomerase I (Top I), a type IB topoisomerase, plays a critical role in relaxing supercoils and mitigating the topological strain associated with transcription. While several proteins from the transcription machinery have been reported to interact with yeast Top I, the precise structural domains involved and the detailed features of the interaction interfaces remain largely unexplored. This gap is partly
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and molecular dynamics to model how yeast topoisomerase I (Top I) interacts with Rpc82, a subunit of RNA polymerase III, in order to relieve transcription-associated torsional stress. The authors identify putative interaction interfaces and structural domains that may mediate this partnership, offering hypotheses for how Top I is recruited to active transcription sites. The work is purely in-silico and provides a structural framework to guide future experimental validation.
